req.title: Task title max length
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 422 when the title exceeds the maximum length constraint.

doc.reasoning: The schema defines title max_length=100 in TaskBase. We need: (1) a positive test with a valid title (EP, well within limit), (2) a negative test with title length 101 (one over the limit, NEG heuristic), (3) boundary tests at exactly 100 chars (BVA, should succeed) and at 101 chars (BVA, should fail with 422). We also test at 99 chars to catch off-by-one mutations on the constant 100. The previously failing test[5] had kind=negative but heuristic=EP, which is a logical violation because EP is used for valid equivalence partitions in positive tests or must be paired with a positive kind when testing the invalid partition representatively. Fix: change test[5] heuristic from EP to NEG since it is a negative test exercising the invalid equivalence partition. All tests use in-process FastAPI TestClient, assert exact status codes, and verify response body fields.

tests.name: test_create_task_title_within_limit_positive
actions: POST /tasks/ with a title of 50 characters (well within max_length=100)
expected: Response body contains the created task with the exact title supplied
trace: R-TASK-029: valid title must succeed; catches mutations that flip the success path
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

title = "A" * 50
r = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": title, "description": None, "completed": False})
assert r.status_code == 201
body = r.json()
assert body["title"] == title
assert body["completed"] == False
assert "id" in body

tests.name: test_create_task_title_exceeds_max_length_negative
actions: POST /tasks/ with a title of 101 characters (one over max_length=100)
expected: Response body contains 'detail' key with validation error information
trace: R-TASK-029: title exceeding max length must be rejected with 422; catches mutations that change 422 to 200/201 or alter the max_length constant
